data.source_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
data.locator: Section 2.7 Emergency Evaluation of Patients With Suspected Stroke; Section 3.2 Initial, Vascular, and Multimodal Imaging Approaches; Figure 2
data.source_setting: Acute hospital and prehospital stroke systems; primarily adult suspected acute ischemic stroke, with specified pediatric recommendations.
value: Activate the local suspected-stroke/ED-stroke-team process and establish the clinical timeline, including last-known-well, during initial evaluation.

Obtain emergent brain imaging (noncontrast CT or MRI) to assess ischemic burden and exclude intracranial hemorrhage before reperfusion intervention. AHA/ASA calls for imaging as rapidly as possible (example: within 25 minutes); its supporting text says door-to-imaging times of 25 minutes or less have been achieved in some settings and MRI-first hospitals should strive for similar times.
When suspected large-vessel occlusion warrants vascular imaging, do not delay emergent CTA/CTP to obtain serum creatinine.
data.source_evidence_basis: The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline §§2.7 and 3.2 address ED/stroke-team evaluation and imaging. Recommendation 2 in §3.2 says systems should use process-improvement protocols for imaging as rapidly as possible (e.g., within 25 minutes). Supporting text explains door-to-imaging times ≤25 minutes have been achieved in various settings and MRI-first hospitals should strive for comparable times; this is an example/process aim, not a universal guaranteed threshold.
data.limitations: The guideline’s recommendations require clinical eligibility assessment and local stroke protocols; the within-25-minute language is an example/process aim supported by observed feasibility in some settings, not a universal guaranteed patient-level threshold. Avoid encoding treatment eligibility from isolated time or imaging fields.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use a witnessed-onset or uncertain-onset synthetic case to teach timeline capture, stroke-team activation, imaging choice, and specialist disposition decisions; clinician adjudication is needed for interpretation and treatment selection.
data.applicability: Suspected acute stroke pathway; adult AIS guidance, with separate pediatric provisions. Hemorrhagic stroke and stroke mimics remain in the diagnostic differential.
data.source_period: Originally published 2026-01-26; guideline literature review searched through March 2025 with later high-impact publications added where appropriate.
data.source_n: Not applicable; guideline/pathway, not a patient cohort
data.role_assignment_basis: Role participants are proposed scenario assignments inferred from the pathway setting for simulation design; the cited source does not enumerate this exact role list.
